task_brief: This is day 7 of "Sharing My Work: Portfolio and Choice Showcase". That is unit 6 in grade 3. Today is an investigation about choosing favorite work. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Assemble and share, privately, in writing, or with an audience of choice, a portfolio of favorite work from the year with short reflections. Today helps by working on choosing favorite work. Your unit also covers choosing favorite work, writing about my work, practicing a presentation, and giving and receiving feedback. Today adds real evidence toward your unit project.
primary_task: Look closely at an artwork about choosing favorite work that you did not make. Describe it first. Do not judge it yet. What is there? How is it put together? What happens as you look or listen? Now say what it makes you feel and which exact part does that. Point to something a reader could check. Last, write one question the artwork makes you wonder. REFERENCE WORK — Mini-portfolio "Routes." Item A: three pencil thumbnails testing path direction. Item B: a four-event notated sound pattern testing repetition. Item C: a one-page reflection comparing which revision clarified intent. Sequence rationale: question → experiment → evidence. Rights log: every item is an Academy-original example. Access note: each item has a text description and may be reviewed privately. Use it to study choosing favorite work; describe evidence before judging and adapt the example rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. critique_criteria: You described it before judging it.
Everything you said points to something a reader could check in the artwork.
You named the exact part that creates the feeling.
You wrote one question the artwork made you wonder.
The artwork is free to use or properly credited, and you used only a small part.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.

task_accessibility_provisions: You never have to perform in front of people. Showing one trusted grown-up, or just writing about it, counts the same.

You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

remediation: Reteaching for choosing favorite work follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for choosing favorite work, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for choosing favorite work works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of choosing favorite work, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking choosing favorite work mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply choosing favorite work under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on choosing favorite work rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
